concerns.text: FR-005 states the system MUST construct a structure‑aware graph, but the unresolved comments explicitly defer FR‑005 because no open CIF dataset is available, creating a direct contradiction between a mandatory requirement and a declared deferral.

FR-006 requires calculation of the performance gap (ΔR²) between composition‑only and structure‑aware models, yet FR‑005 (the structure‑aware baseline) is deferred, making FR‑006 impossible to satisfy.
Success Criterion SC-002 demands measurement and reporting of ΔR², but the required baseline (FR‑005/FR‑006) is deferred, so the criterion cannot be met.
FR-001 (and several other FRs) reference “US-1” (e.g., “See US-1”), but no identifier US‑1 is defined anywhere in the document, leaving the cross‑reference unresolved.
FR-002 also cites “US-1” without a defined US‑1, causing an undefined reference.
FR-003 mentions “See US-1” yet US‑1 does not exist in the spec.
FR-004 includes “See US-1” but the referenced user story identifier is missing.
FR-007 cites “See US-1” without a defined US‑1.
FR-009 also points to “See US-1”, which is undefined.
FR-005 cites “See US-2”, yet no US‑2 identifier is defined in the document.
FR-006 cites “See US-2” without a defined US‑2.

FR-005 requires constructing structure-aware graphs from CIF files, but the spec does not guarantee that the necessary CIF files are available in the Materials Project Open Data subset. Without reachable CIF inputs, FR-005 (and consequently SC-002 which depends on a structure-aware baseline) cannot be exercised, making these requirements untestable.

The specification defers implementation of FR-005 (structure‑aware graph construction) and FR-006 (ΔR² calculation) while still asserting that a performance‑gap ΔR² will be reported. This makes the central research question—quantifying information loss when crystal‑structure data is excluded—empirically unanswerable, constituting a scientific flaw.

FR-005 (structure‑aware graph construction) is marked as **deferred** and no implementation task is provided, yet the core research question and SC-002 require a structure‑aware baseline to quantify information loss. Without this baseline the primary claim (ΔR²) is untestable.
FR-006 (calculate metrics and ΔR² between composition‑only and structure‑aware models) is also deferred; the plan contains no task to compute the performance gap, making SC-002 impossible to satisfy.
SC-002 demands reporting of the ΔR² performance gap, but the required structure‑aware baseline is omitted (see FR-005/FR-006). This leaves the central scientific contribution undefined.

FR-008 proposes correlating PCA components of node embeddings with periodic properties that are *already used as input node features* (electronegativity, atomic radius, etc.). Such a correlation is trivially expected and constitutes a circular validation; the analysis must use properties not used in the model inputs.

FR-007 states that confidence intervals for predictions are calculated as mean ± 1.96 × std derived from R² scores across folds. R² is a goodness‑of‑fit statistic, not a measure of prediction variance, so this method for confidence intervals is statistically inappropriate.

The specification defers implementation of FR-005 (structure‑aware graph construction) and FR-006 (ΔR² calculation) while still asserting that a performance‑gap ΔR² will be reported. This makes the central research question—quantifying information loss when crystal‑structure data is excluded—empirically unanswerable, constituting a scientific flaw.

new_concerns.text: FR-009 specifies that a 30‑minute per‑epoch timeout should log a warning and *continue*, while the US‑1 acceptance scenario 3 expects the job to *halt* on the same condition. This contradiction makes the required behavior ambiguous and thus untestable. Clarify whether the system should continue after an epoch timeout or halt execution.

responses.response: Provided concrete implementation tasks for the structure‑aware baseline (FR-005) and the performance‑gap calculation (FR-006), added a new requirement (FR-011) to download publicly available CIF files from the Materials Project API, and clarified SC-002 to reflect the now‑implemented ΔR² metric. This resolves the scientific flaw by ensuring the ΔR² gap can be measured with an open dataset.
